title: Time and sequence
subtitle: as soon as, while, after that, eventually
summary: Link events in time: say what happens first, what happens at the same time, and what happens in the end.

lesson.heading: when and as soon as
lesson.text: **When** and **as soon as** have almost the same meaning, but **as soon as** sounds more immediate or more important. After both of them we use a present tense, never a future form.

examples.text: I'll phone my uncle **when** I get home.
**As soon as** you've finished this exercise, you can go home.
I'll see you **when** I get there.

lesson.note: We do not use will after when or as soon as.

lesson.heading: Two things at the same time: while, as, just as
lesson.text: Use **while** for two longer actions, or for a short action inside a longer one. Use **(just) as** for two short actions that happen at the same moment.

examples.text: Violet got ready **while** I cooked the dinner.
The accident happened **while** I was on my way to work.
examples.note: a short action inside a long one; when or as are also possible

examples.text: I saw him **just as** I came out of the office.
examples.note: two short actions; when is also possible

lesson.heading: One thing after another
lesson.text: **Then**, **after that** and **afterwards** all mean *later*. After **after** and **before** we use the *-ing* form of the verb, not the infinitive.

examples.text: We met the others in the cafe, and **then** we went to the match.
I talked to Joe, and **afterwards** I came home.
examples.note: = at a later time, usually the same day

examples.text: I was in Caracas for three months, and **after that** I went to Colombia.
**After** seeing the film, we went home.
We had something to eat **before** going out.

lesson.heading: A sequence of actions
lesson.text: To tell a story in order, start with **first of all** (or **first**), continue with **then** or **after that**, and introduce the last thing with **finally**.

examples.text: **First of all** we spent a few days in St Moritz.
**After that** we drove down the coast and stayed in Portofino for a week.
**Finally**, we went back to Switzerland to stay with my uncle.

lesson.heading: From the beginning to the end
rows: in the first period of time
finally, after a long time or a lot of problems
finally, after a period of time or a lot of thought

lesson.heading: A story from beginning to end
lesson.text: These phrases often work together in one story: you start with **to begin with** or **at first**, add **after a while**, and close with **eventually** or **in the end**.

examples.text: **To begin with**, the two girls got on very well when they shared the flat.
But **after a while** they started arguing, and **eventually** Lauren walked out.
**At first** I enjoyed the classes, but **in the end** I left.

lesson.heading: A list of reasons
lesson.text: To give a first reason, say **firstly**, **for one thing** or **for a start**. To add another reason, say **secondly**, **besides** or **anyway**.

examples.text: *A:* What's wrong with her new dress? *B:* **Firstly**, it's a horrible colour, and **secondly**, I don't think it suits her.
*A:* Why can't we go out tonight? *B:* Well, **for one thing**, I've got a lot of work - and **besides**, I can't afford it.

lesson.text: Afterwards stands alone (we went home afterwards), but after that needs the word that; both mean the same.

exercises.prompt: Match the words and phrases that are similar in meaning.
I'll give them your message as soon as I ___ there.
exercises.explanation: We do not use a future form after when or as soon as.

exercises.prompt: Maria cleaned the kitchen ___ I did the bathroom.
exercises.explanation: Two long actions at the same time take while.

exercises.prompt: The phone rang ___ I was shutting the front door.
exercises.explanation: Two short actions at the same moment take just as.
After and before are followed by the -ing form.

exercises.prompt: Before ___ they went to an exhibition in a little gallery.
exercises.explanation: After before we use the -ing form.

exercises.prompt: Well, first of all we flew to Lisbon. After that we took the train to Lagos. And ___ we went to Faro and flew home.
exercises.explanation: Finally introduces the last item in a sequence.

exercises.prompt: ___ I think he found India difficult, because the food and weather are so different. But after a while he got used to it.
exercises.explanation: At first and to begin with describe the first period of time.

exercises.prompt: But after a ___ he got used to it, and didn't want to come home.
exercises.explanation: After a while = after a period of time.

exercises.prompt: The company did well at first. But then the manager left, they started losing money, and ___ they had to close down.
exercises.explanation: Eventually = finally, after a long time or a lot of problems.

exercises.prompt: Does the phrase point to the start of a story or to the end?
Put the words in order to give two reasons for staying in.
words: I'd like to watch a programme
exercises.answer: For one thing I'd like to watch a programme and besides I don't think it'll be a good party
exercises.explanation: For one thing introduces the first reason; besides adds another.

exercises.statement: I'll text you as soon as I will arrive.
exercises.explanation: I'll text you as soon as I arrive. We never use will after as soon as.
